slides.big: In 5 years, nobody at work will remember the nights you stayed late.
slides.small: Your kids will remember every single one.

slides.big: You did it so they'd see you as reliable.
slides.small:
The late nights.
The 9 PM texts.
The "I'll handle it."
Brick by brick, you built a reputation.

When you leave, that reputation stays in the building.
Your desk has a new name within weeks.

slides.big: So what actually comes home with you?
slides.small:
Whatever's left.
The short temper. The silence.
The guy who's "just tired."

You can't always quit.
But you can stop giving the job what it never paid for.
slides.small:
Do the work. Leave on time.
Be all the way home.

In 5 years, nobody at work will remember the nights you stayed late. Your kids will. 👇

You built a reputation one late night at a time. The guy who never says no. The guy who always picks up.

But that reputation stays in the building when you leave. What comes home is whatever's left of you.

You can't always walk away from the job. You can stop handing it the hours it never paid for.

Who's getting the best of YOU right now, work or home? Be honest. 👇

slides.big: Your boss isn't thinking about you at 10 PM.
slides.small: So why are you still thinking about him?

The meeting. The tone. The look.
The "we need to talk."
In the shower. In bed. At your kid's game.

That's a micromanager who followed you home.
And you let him live there rent-free.
Every hour he lives in your head is an hour your family gets a version of you that isn't really there.

1. Write tomorrow's worries on paper before you leave.
2. When the replay starts, say "That's for tomorrow."
3. Change clothes the minute you get home.
